doc.title: John Bunch interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Gene Krupa's kindness and the Zildjian cymbals
summary: Krupa rehearsed at Bunch's apartment and later got him a set of hand-picked cymbals.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: Well I can’t think of many stories in relation to those two. I’m not a very good, I don’t have a very good memory. As far as, I was just telling some people today you know I also worked with Gene Krupa quite a lot in the quartet. With Charlie Ventura. He was one of the great guys, one of the nicest guys, personally. The complete opposite from these three guys that I worked long periods of time on. And I should put in a word, speaking of nice guys that had fame and everything, Woody Herman was another one that I worked for, and they were both great. Now Gene, Gene was here’s an example of how nice he was. When I got that job we couldn’t find any, there was nothing written down for that quartet, it had to be memorized. So we had to have a rehearsal for my benefit. And we couldn’t find, things were very busy in New York then and you couldn’t find a rehearsal hall just at the drop of a hat like that, and I said, well if you don’t mind, come up to my place, I have a Steinway grand and I have a set of drums, I had a bass even. Because I used to like to have jam sessions at my apartment. And he asked me about the drums, and I said they are Slingerland drums, which that was his company, and he said okay, I’ll bring the cymbals and we’ll rehearse up at your place. So we came up there and when he was up there he says what kind of cymbals do you have? And I showed him mine and he didn’t say anything. And a year or two passed and I started working with him and a year or two passed. And one time we were in Boston and we met Zildjian who is the great cymbal maker. Just out of the clear blue he says, “hey, why don’t you give John Bunch some cymbals? Send John Bunch some cymbals. He’s got a nice set of drums but he doesn’t have very good cymbals.” He remembered that. So I didn’t think anything, I thought oh, nothing will ever happen. And about two or three weeks later I get a big special package, very heavy, full of these cymbals. The best cymbals, hand picked by Zildjian himself, thanks to Gene. I mean it was just the kind of a guy he was, you know. So, you know, oh and when I unwrapped them they were sort of dirty looking and I’m thinking, not knowing anything about drums, I thought oh, you didn’t give me nice new cymbals. And I showed them to, I think it was Jake Hanna or somebody, and he said, “My, those are wonderful cymbals,” he says, “hand picked, they’re perfect.” They were worth, I don’t know, a lot of money. He says, “You can’t find cymbals like that.” So anyhow, thanks to Gene I got all these wonderful things and the memory, I mean, that he could remember that you know. To take time to remember something.
